gang.name: Samuel Gregg
gang.rel: rode with you in the war
gang.pitch: He has killed men and sleeps fine.

gang.name: Cole Younger
gang.pitch: Rode with Quantrill. Big, clever, proud, and he wants a fair share.

gang.name: Ike Bassham
gang.pitch: A farm boy who wants more than a mule and a plough.

gang.name: Jasper Lockhart
gang.pitch: Steals horses in Kansas and sells them in Missouri. Can ride anything.

gang.name: Henry Hulse
gang.pitch: Rode with Shelby. Cannot find work that does not involve a Yankee boss.

gang.name: Zeke Askew
gang.pitch: Has killed two men in Texas. Wants a name of his own.

offers.name: Frank Ballard
offers.pitch: Cool hands at a card table and at a bank counter.

offers.name: Clint Holt
offers.pitch: A farm boy who wants more than a mule and a plough.

offers.name: Otis Price
offers.pitch: Knows every story about you by heart and asks too many questions.

lastJob.name: State Savings Bank, St. Joseph
beats: 3 of you drift in by twos, horses tied where they will be needed, and walk in like customers.
Somebody shouts. The alarm is up before the money is out.
You get some of it — the cashier stalls and the rest stays behind.
The town fights. Rifles from the hardware store, shotguns from the upper windows.
A posse forms but loses you in friendly country.
Zeke Askew is hit in the street but stays in the saddle.
Jesse James is hit in the street but stays in the saddle.
lastJob.headline: ST. JOSEPH: BOLD ROBBERY — $4,574 Carried Off

dead.name: Samuel Gregg
dead.how: killed in the street, First National Bank, Kansas City

log.text: The war is over. Not for Jesse James. You are back on the farm in Clay County with Ambrose James, Jesse Lockhart, Samuel Gregg, and none of you means to plough.

log.title: The State
log.text: The Radical legislature keeps the Ironclad Oath: no man who aided the rebellion may vote, preach, teach or practise law. Half of Little Dixie cannot vote.

log.title: A girl from home
log.text: Tell him the gang comes first.
LIBERTY: A QUIET ROBBERY — $2,902 Taken Without a Shot
Cole Younger rides with you now.
RICHMOND: A QUIET ROBBERY — $5,330 Taken Without a Shot

log.title: The State
log.text: Cattle drives from Texas reach Kansas City. The stockyards are full and the saloons are fuller.
Ike Bassham rides with you now.
KANSAS CITY: A QUIET ROBBERY — $5,712 Taken Without a Shot

log.title: The State
log.text: Camp meetings along the Fishing River draw a thousand souls.
Jasper Lockhart rides with you now.
LIBERTY: A QUIET ROBBERY — $5,842 Taken Without a Shot

log.title: The tax collector
log.text: Mark the day.
LEXINGTON: A QUIET ROBBERY — $4,649 Taken Without a Shot

log.title: The State
log.text: Work begins on a railroad bridge over the Missouri at Kansas City. The town that gets the bridge gets the West.
KANSAS CITY: A QUIET ROBBERY — $5,264 Taken Without a Shot
RICHMOND: A QUIET ROBBERY — $5,001 Taken Without a Shot
You marry Zerelda Dalton. Your mother cries, the preacher does not ask questions, and your gang gets drunk.
KANSAS CITY: A QUIET ROBBERY — $9,473 Taken Without a Shot

log.title: The State
log.text: The Missouri is high. Two ferries lost at Lexington.
ST. JOSEPH: CASHIER MURDERED — Bandits Escape With $3,189

log.title: The State
log.text: Grant is elected President. Missouri goes Republican, with most of its rebels barred from the polls.
A Jefferson City lawyer takes your money and your case. He knows the governor's friends.
Henry Hulse rides with you now.
LEXINGTON: A QUIET ROBBERY — $5,442 Taken Without a Shot

log.title: The State
log.text: Wheat brings 1.20 a bushel in St. Louis this season.
LIBERTY: A QUIET ROBBERY — $5,670 Taken Without a Shot

log.title: Family
log.text: Zerelda has a daughter. You name her Lucinda.
KANSAS CITY: A QUIET ROBBERY — $6,654 Taken Without a Shot

log.title: The State
log.text: The Hannibal Bridge opens at Kansas City, the first across the Missouri. Kansas City will outgrow St. Joseph now.
LIBERTY: A QUIET ROBBERY — $5,834 Taken Without a Shot
RICHMOND: BOLD ROBBERY — $3,138 Carried Off
LEXINGTON: A QUIET ROBBERY — $3,994 Taken Without a Shot

John Newman Edwards of the Kansas City Times, who rode with Jo Shelby, has started printing letters from Missouri's "outlaws" and defending them as Southern men driven to it. He will print yours. (After a job you can write to him: legend and Southern sympathy rise, and so does the reward.)
log.title: A friend at the Kansas City Times
Family
log.text: Zerelda has a son. You name him Cole.
John Newman Edwards prints your letter: you are a Southern man wronged by Radicals, and you name the men who can swear where you were that day.
KANSAS CITY: BOLD ROBBERY — $4,643 Carried Off
Another letter in the Kansas City Times. Even friends say you should stop writing to the papers.
Zeke Askew rides with you now.
LIBERTY: A QUIET ROBBERY — $4,575 Taken Without a Shot

log.title: The State
log.text: The Liberal Republicans and the Democrats carry the state for Gratz Brown. The test oath is struck down; ex-Confederates vote again.

log.title: A preacher speaks against you
log.text: Give $100 to his church.
